rich_narrative.summary: The International Institute of Islamic Thought (IIIT) faces significant operational and reporting limitations. No financial filings newer than FY2023 are available — donors should treat this 3-year-old financial picture with caution [12]. The organization focuses on academic research and capacity building, publishing scholarly texts such as <cite id="3">over 600 scholarly titles</cite> and running initiatives like Advancing Education in Muslim Societies [12]. However, revenue sharply declined from <cite id="12">$16,355,779 in FY2022</cite> to <cite id="12">$8,955,918 in FY2023</cite>, reflecting a 45% drop in funding [12]. Furthermore, <cite id="12">95.0% of expenses remain within the United States</cite> despite an international mission mandate [12]. While the organization maintained a <cite id="12">96.6% program expense ratio in 2023</cite>, its lack of a documented theory of change and missing current financial disclosures severely limit donor visibility [12].
